text:
tessa: Heads up — our FastAPI sample that creates httpx.AsyncClient at module import is causing sporadic test failures in CI (windows runners) and noisy "RuntimeError: Event loop is closed" traces during teardown. anyone have quick tips?

joel: We hit this before. Two main problems: creating AsyncClient at import means it tries to start background tasks on import when there's no running loop (or the loop is different in pytest/xdist workers). Also uvicorn --reload/--workers can fork processes causing double-init.

tessa: Repro is easy: import clients.py in a test module, run pytest -n auto and sometimes the worker fails with "Task was destroyed but it is pending" and sometimes Event loop closed.

ravi: For CI we solved it by making the client a lazily-created singleton that's tied to asyncio.get_running_loop(). But that's brittle on Windows where the default loop policy changed. I'd suggest explicit async fixtures instead.

joel: Agree. Minimal fix for samples: show the client created inside an async lifespan or dependency. Example snippet we added to our internal samples:
```python
# app/__init__.py
from fastapi import FastAPI
from httpx import AsyncClient

app = FastAPI()

@app.on_event('startup')
async def start_client():
    app.state.api_client = AsyncClient(base_url='https://api')

@app.on_event('shutdown')
async def close_client():
    await app.state.api_client.aclose()
```
Then endpoints use request.app.state.api_client
```

ravi: For tests use an async fixture that creates the client against the ASGI app (httpx.AsyncClient(app=app)), yields it, then aclose. That avoids loop races and doesn't require network.

tessa: Any idea if we should change our public Python SDK to help avoid this? A lot of newcomers copy-paste the simple example with client = AsyncClient() at top-level.

joel: Maybe add a runtime warning in the SDK constructor if no running loop is found — something like: "AsyncClient instantiated outside of async context, ensure you close it or use an async context manager" — but be careful: we don't want to spam logs for valid patterns. Could gate the warning to when an aclose wasn't scheduled on program exit.

ravi: Another safer pattern for SDK: provide a helper context manager factory in sdk.utils, e.g. sdk.utils.async_client_context(base_url) that yields an asynccontextmanager. Then samples reference that helper so users are less likely to mis-use httpx directly.

tessa: We also saw issues with pytest's collection phase importing the app which triggers client creation before pytest-asyncio sets up the loop. So don't import client objects at module scope in tests.

joel: For Windows specifically, setting the event loop policy to asyncio.WindowsSelectorEventLoopPolicy in test setup helped when we used subprocess-based runners, but prefer to avoid that magic.

ci-bot: Created issue #617: "python-sdk: sample app top-level AsyncClient causes flaky tests and event loop errors". Link: https://git.internal/redwood/devex/issues/617

tessa: I'll open a docs PR replacing top-level client samples with lifespan + pytest fixture examples, and add a short note about uvicorn --reload and pytest-xdist. Thanks for the pointers.

ravi: Happy to review the PR. Also good to mention httpx transport details (background ping tasks) as a cause.

joel: Could also add a short lint in our examples CI that runs pytest on the sample to catch regressions.

tessa: Added to my TODOs. I'll include a tiny repro test that demonstrates the warning so reviewers can see the failure locally. Thanks :slightly_smiling_face:
